_comment: Canonical defect register — closure criterion G2.3 (`docs/PROJECT-CLOSURE-GATE.md` §5, owner ruling 6). Repository-local and version-controlled on purpose: GitHub Issues are explicitly NOT canonical, because closure must not depend on an external tracker being reachable. Issues may mirror this file. PASS = zero OPEN P0/P1 rows. Read it with `aisef.control.defects:read` — the same reader the closure probe uses, so a report and the gate cannot disagree. This file is missing = UNRUNNABLE at closure; this file present with an empty `defects` = a real PASS.
_boundary: `docs/FAILURE-TAXONOMY.md` answers *what went wrong and what did we learn* (133 closed rows: symptom, root cause, lesson, fix). This register answers *what is outstanding now, at what severity*. A defect sits here while open and there once understood, and a row here points at its taxonomy row by id instead of restating it — nothing is copied in either direction. Work that is wanted but whose absence is not a wrong result (the POST_CLOSE list in the contract's §7, `docs/ROADMAP-POST-1.0.md`) is not a defect and is not entered here.
_fields: id (stable, never reused) · severity (P0–P3, scale below) · status (OPEN | CLOSED) · title · introduced / fixed (version or commit, where known; empty when it is not) · evidence (the regression test, or the command that recomputes the measurement) · check (optional: the `gate.CHECK_NAMES` entry the defect bears on) · taxonomy (optional: the FAILURE-TAXONOMY.md row id) · notes. No timestamps: the file must digest the same on every read or G2.3's staleness detection reads noise as change.

severity_scale._comment: Reused by reference, never redefined here. P0 = cannot install, data loss, security issue, incorrect gate result. P1 = cannot complete the lifecycle without author assistance. P2 = significant confusion / DX friction. P3 = cosmetic or optional. The reader refuses a register that names another source or edits `blocking`.

defects.title: A test run with no readable results records other stories' requirements as regressions
defects.evidence: python3 validation/o3_preservation_radius.py → `todo: 4 scored stories, 36 behaviours, 2 confirmed regressors, 4 uncorroborated REOPENED` (FR-1, FR-2, FR-4 owned by STORY-02-01 and FR-9 by STORY-01-02, all flipped by STORY-02-02 at at=1788947583.932249, an event whose `test` tool_run is ok=True exit_code=0 with `test_format: ""`, `test_ids: []`, `failed_ids: []`). No regression test yet.
defects.notes:
Same class as taxonomy row 155 (absence read as regression), in the branch that fix did not cover: `ledger._observe_tests`, when `readable` is false, calls `rollup(line, False, why)` for the home story, so every requirement that story `covers` — owned by earlier, VERIFIED stories — is observed not-green and `observe` records REOPENED. Nothing red was read anywhere. P1 and not P2 because the loop's own arithmetic is corrupted by it (`improve` stops on Δverified − Δreopened) and only a human comparing the ledger against the evidence can tell the artifact from a regression; P1 and not P0 because no gate verdict is demonstrably wrong on disk — the mechanism by which one could be (a behaviour REOPENED by another story is dropped from that story's `preservation` list, `complexity.verified_touched`) is real but was never reached here: STORY-02-02 was the last story of that corpus and it failed. The trigger is not exotic — any project whose test output AISEF cannot parse yields `test_format: ""`. false_pass=false: false FAIL, not false PASS: an unreadable test run marks other stories' requirements REOPENED — it invents a regression, it does not pass a defect. Lives in the ledger projection, not in a gate check.
CLOSED 2026-09-14. The fix is the removal of one call: `rollup(line, False, why)` in the `not readable` branch of `ledger._observe_tests`. The per-criterion `note()`s stay -- not reading a test name genuinely means this story has proven nothing, and `gap_kind` classifies those as UNTRACED. What is gone is flipping OTHER stories' requirements: a requirement is a shared cross-story artifact and must not change status because one run could not be read.
No false-PASS risk, and this is the reason the fix is safe rather than merely small: an unreadable run only ever passed `False`, so removing the call can prevent a false REOPENED and cannot produce a VERIFIED.
Measured before and after on the four todo* corpora with `python3 validation/o3_preservation_radius.py`: `todo` goes from 4 uncorroborated REOPENED to 0, the other three were already 0, and the confirmed-regressor counts are unchanged (todo-oc 4, todo-cli 5, todo 2, todo-e2e 4; 15 of 32 stories). Real regression detection is therefore intact -- the negative control is in `tests/test_ledger.py::TestKhongDocDuocKhongPhaiHoiQuy::test_mot_phep_thu_do_that_van_lam_reopened`.
taxonomy stays 155: this is the same failure class (absence read as regression) in a branch that fix did not cover, and the register's rule is to point at a taxonomy row, never to restate or duplicate it.

defects.title: A blocking gate decision can rest on the model reviewer alone
defects.evidence: python3 bin/aisef closure -> G2.4b: 17 of 122 blocks judge-alone (13.9 %), all four properties hold; closure-evidence/judge-only-audit.json (2026-09-14) carries the per-property assertions. SUPERSEDED FIGURE: this row previously quoted 36.8 % (21 of 57) from `aisef.control.reviewer_qual` over the four todo* corpora. That measurement predates defect 158, which took the blocking-line parse rate from 0/177 to 116/177 -- `Finding.id` could not be computed on real reviewer output at all when it was taken. The old number is kept here in words, not deleted, because the published O1 report still carries it and docs/O1-RECOMPUTE-AFTER-158.md is the dated addendum that reconciles them. Lifecycle effect, same corpus: todo-e2e STORY-... ended `failed` on the judge's word with no deterministic check disagreeing.
defects.notes:
Closure criterion G2.4b owns the verdict on this fact (REQUIRED_WITH_WAIVER_ALLOWED, owner ruling 1: no reviewer redesign for closure's sake, and the measured rate stays a published property).
P1 -> P2 on 2026-09-14. The P1 rested on one argument: that the contract's exemption for the model-judge error rate is conditional on 'no blocking decision rests on the judge alone', and that condition does not hold. Owner ruling 1 REPLACED that blanket condition with four named properties -- a judge-only block must be explicitly identifiable in evidence, distinguishable from deterministic blocking, have a human escape/override path, and be unable to masquerade as a deterministic guarantee. G2.4b now PASSES on exactly those four, without a waiver, so the owner's stated test is met and the P1's own justification is superseded by the ruling it was written under. This row's earlier note anticipated the reading ('the argument for P2 is owner ruling 1 read as also excusing it from G2.3'); the ruling settled it.
NOT closed: judge-alone blocks still exist (17 of 122) and the rate remains a published property of the framework, so the fact stays on the register. P2 is the honest severity for a measured property that blocks nothing and sets no gate -- it does not gate G2.3, and it is not being waived, which are different things.
false_pass=false throughout: a judge-only block is a blocking decision resting on a model-judge check, not a deterministic or structural check passing when it should fail.

defects.title: `_analyze.cut_sessions` merges two bench cohorts on the three tasks they share
defects.evidence: tests/bench/_analyze.py: `_DUONG_DAN_PHIEN = re.compile(r"\.bench[\w.-]*/run/([\w-]+)/([\w-]+)/a(\d+)")` matches any ledger directory but captures only (condition, task, attempt), so `.bench/run/…` and `.bench-c1b/run/…` land on one key. Recorded in docs/BENCH-TASK-DISCRIMINATION.md §6 with the three affected tasks (`sec-1`, `sec-2`, `state-3`).
defects.notes: Deliberately not fixed: both published bench reports quote this function's output, so re-keying it makes a re-run of `analyze` print a table that differs from the printed evidence. P2 — the wrong number is an auxiliary cut-session count in a bench analysis helper, it blocks nothing and sets no gate. The contract lists it POST_CLOSE (§7); that is a scheduling statement, and P2 is the severity — they agree, and neither is derived from the other. false_pass=false: a bench analysis counter, not a gate check at all.

defects.title: criterion identity is positional, so a test can silently become proof for a different criterion
defects.introduced: pre-dates this wave; surfaced 2026-09-14 by the marks-cli closure corpus
defects.evidence: marks-cli _bmad-output/plan-reconciliation.json §incomplete_withdrawal.how_the_agent_resolved_it; tests named AC-STORY-01-02-1 in marks-cli tests/dispatch.test.js now assert STORY-02-02 `list` behaviour while that code maps to 'unknown verb exits 1'; AC-STORY-01-02-4 is orphaned
defects.notes:
false_pass=true: `criteria have tests` is a blocking STRUCTURAL check and a shifted test satisfies it while proving another behaviour. First registered true false PASS, so G2.4a moved PASSED -> FAILED; owner decision 2026-09-14 was that it stays FAILED until fixed, not waived and not weakened. Not preventable by instruction: the developer never sees the criterion list, so the fix had to be a detector plus a stable identity, not a convention.
CLOSED 2026-09-14 in two commits, against the owner's five acceptance points:
  (1) delete/reorder cannot silently change identity — identity is now the pair (code, content digest); `acceptance.drift()` names the codes whose criterion text moved. Reorder is the case a count cannot see: same count, nothing orphaned, each test proving the other's criterion.
  (2) a test cannot silently become proof for another criterion — same digest pair; for a story already merged DONE, `run._done_criteria_drift` compares the recorded contract note against today's criteria and the epic STOPS instead of skipping it silently. Re-running cannot repair that case: the work is on the main branch, so the developer would open an already-green tree (bug 143's measured failure).
  (3) orphaned AC ids detected — `acceptance.orphans()`, blocking in the gate.
  (4) duplicate/mismatched mappings detected — `acceptance.overloaded()` blocks a test whose name carries two codes of one story (two criteria, one behaviour: no count sees it, `missing` is empty and nothing is orphaned). Separately, the register's `check_kind` is now DERIVED from `gate.CHECK_KIND` and a hand-written kind that contradicts the framework reads UNRUNNABLE — declaring a structural false PASS as `model-judge` was itself a way past G2.4a.
  (5) the gate cannot PASS `criteria have tests` on drifted identity — orphans and ambiguous mappings block there; drift is caught at plan level because within one attempt the criteria and the note are the same text by construction, so a drift comparison inside `evaluate()` could never fire.
No baseline reads as CANNOT DECIDE, never as fine — merging those two is the same false-PASS class. The note is therefore also written when an existing one lacks the digest map, so corpora that already have work to lose acquire a baseline.
Corpus status: the identity sweep over all 7 marks-cli stories finds exactly one residual problem, STORY-01-02's orphaned AC-STORY-01-02-4 — a present-state defect the replay cannot see, because ADR-005 V4 replays with the acceptance count recorded at that attempt (4), which was correct then. G4 evidence stays not-closure-valid until that orphan is resolved, at 7/7 or not.

defects.title: a 401 names the credential source but not the client and model that failed
defects.introduced: pre-dates this wave; surfaced 2026-09-14 by a misdiagnosis in this repository
defects.evidence: marks-cli _bmad-output/evidence/STORY-04-01.jsonl: six agent_run records carry client=opencode model=9router/mycombo session_id=ses_*; the failing record carries client=claude model=claude-opus-5[1m] session_id=<uuid> exit_status=auth. The error string named ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and nothing else, and was read as 'the project's key rotated' -- on a project whose ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json sets disabled_providers: ["anthropic"]. Probed after the fix: GET /v1/models -> 200, POST /v1/chat/completions model=mycombo -> 200 resolving downstream to MiniMax-M3.
defects.notes:
auth_hint listed whichever AUTH_ENV_NAMES were present in the child environment and asserted they were used. Presence in the shell is not evidence of use. It was only called from claude_code.py, so the sentence was true of the session it described -- but it described the credential SOURCE, not the PATH, and on a project with more than one client configured only the client and model attribute a 401 to a request. The opencode adapter had no auth branch at all, so a genuine 9router rejection produced a bare line the operator could not act on.
Fixed: auth_hint takes client and model and names them first; environment variables are named only for clients that actually read them (ENV_AUTH_CLIENTS), so an opencode failure never points at an Anthropic variable the request never touched; the opencode adapter now produces the message too. The hint also says that a wrong --client is a likelier cause than a rotated key, which is what actually happened.
Severity P2: it sets no gate and passes no check -- it cost a wrong diagnosis and a wasted report, not a wrong verdict.

defects.title: a credential rejection is charged against the story's quality attempts
defects.introduced: pre-dates this wave; surfaced 2026-09-14 on the marks-cli corpus
defects.evidence: marks-cli run.log 2026-09-14 12:58:44: `attempt=1 FAIL ... attempt=2 START` on a 401 whose session note records moved_tree: false and 'auth and the tree is untouched -- nothing to grade'. quality_attempts counts attempts where not a.infra, and `auth` is not in INFRA_STATUSES, so the story spent quality budget on a session the agent had no part in.
defects.notes:
`auth` is kept OUT of INFRA_STATUSES deliberately and that reasoning is sound and measured: a rejected credential is not transient, so retrying spends the infra budget on a failure that repeats identically (2026-09-12: 176 s per attempt, $0, three attempts, nothing learned). The defect is that excluding it did not achieve the stated intent -- it only moved the cost to the QUALITY budget and retried anyway. Classifying a status controls accounting, not whether a retry happens; the comment assumed it controlled both.
Fixed with the idiom already in the same function for 'not the agent's fault AND retrying is pointless', which the isolation branch uses: infra=True (nothing was ever scored, so no quality attempt is charged) plus fatal=True (stop now). `auth` stays out of INFRA_STATUSES, so the measured no-retry finding is preserved.
Same shape as taxonomy row 130, which measured it for max_turns: a story spending its whole budget without ever producing a verdict leaves the next developer no feedback.

defects.title: closure bookkeeping bound to a commit can never be current once it is itself committed
defects.evidence: Measured on this repository: suite.json recorded at 9fe6d6f, committing it moved HEAD to 91781e8, and G2.1 read UNRUNNABLE 'recorded at 9fe6d6f, HEAD is 91781e8'. Leaving it uncommitted instead makes the tree dirty, and `closure.pin_target` refuses a dirty tree. `git diff --name-only 9fe6d6f..HEAD` listed only closure-evidence/*.json -- no source file changed.
defects.notes:
A contradiction the closure machinery created for itself, and it blocked the last step of closing the project: 'G2.1/G2.2/G5.4 green' and 'closure_target_sha pinnable' were mutually exclusive, because `closure-evidence/` is tracked and recording evidence is itself a commit.
The measurement interfered with what it measured: the probe asks whether the evidence describes the current SOURCE, but decided it by comparing HEAD's SHA, which moves because of the act of recording.
The same trap exists at `closure_target_sha`, which `pin_target` writes into `docs/closure-gate.json`: committing the pin moves HEAD past the very commit just pinned, so G1.0's second conjunct (HEAD is still the target) fails immediately after pinning, and not committing leaves the tree dirty which `pin_target` refuses. Same loop, different file -- found by testing for it rather than waiting for it to bite at release time.
Fixed narrowly: a commit touching ONLY closure bookkeeping (`closure-evidence/` or the criteria file) changes no source line, so the evidence still describes the tree. Any file outside that directory still invalidates it, and an unreadable diff reads as stale -- the negative control (`test_commit_dung_ma_nguon_thi_bang_chung_cu`) asserts a real source change is still caught.
P1 not P2: it blocked closure outright. false_pass=false -- it produced a false UNRUNNABLE, which blocks; it never let anything through.

defects.title: a CLI whose requirements say it has no UI is treated as having one
defects.evidence: _project_has_ui(marks-cli) returned True with all 7 stories carrying screens: [] and docs/requirements.md reading 'no server, no network, no ui'. detect_file reports frontend: [], mobile: [], undetermined: ['frontend', ...]; Stack.has_ui counts 'frontend' in undetermined, appended whenever a WEB_MARKER matches. Two matched: 'browser' in 'browser profile' and 'ui' inside the denial 'no ui'.
defects.notes: The gate then demanded browser E2E (Playwright) and accessibility of a command-line tool. General, not corpus-specific: any CLI, library or daemon mentioning the web in passing. Fixed by letting a settled plan answer both ways, which the function's own docstring already argued for; an empty index is still not negative evidence.

defects.title: an inferred verification command is used without checking the tool exists, turning a missing tool into a FAILED check
defects.evidence: marks-cli mutation reported FAILED with 'npm error code EAI_AGAIN … request to https://registry.npmjs.org/stryker failed' because command_for_kind returned _DEFAULTS['node']['mutation'] = 'npx stryker run' unconditionally, while the network-isolated verification sandbox correctly has no network.
defects.notes: P1, and false_pass=false: it is a false FAILED, which blocks rather than lets through — but it inverts what a red gate means, reporting a machine that cannot run a check as a project that failed one. `_UNIVERSAL` six lines below already stated the rule it broke. which(argv[0]) is insufficient for a launcher: argv[0] is npx and npx IS installed, so the check must ask whether the tool resolves project-locally. Host PATH is the wrong question entirely — measured: playwright is on this host's PATH while the Docker run still reported 'tool not installed', because a global npm bin does not exist in the container.

defects.title: a kind the framework proved inapplicable still counts as unconfigured and blocks
defects.evidence: run_suite marks needs_ui kinds 'project has no UI' via result.skipped, and QaReport.unconfigured counts every skipped kind, so release_ready was unreachable for any project without a UI.
defects.notes: Conflates an absence (nobody configured a command — must block) with an answer (the framework derived that the kind cannot apply — must not). It forced the operator to sign a waiver for something already proven mechanically, which drains meaning from every real waiver. Fixed with a distinct `not_applicable` state that is still printed in the report: not applicable never means hidden from the signer.

defects.title: a bench run writes artifacts into the framework repository root, outside its session workspaces
defects.evidence: _bmad-output/ appeared at the AISEF repo root with 36 log lines (17 pytest, 1 ruff) between 18:51 and 19:45, spanning the run, while every session recorded correctly into its own workspace (s1/s6/s7 each hold _bmad-output/run.log with 21-27 lines) — so it is a distinct set, from a call whose --project fell back to the default '.'. Preserved at scratchpad/leaked-bmad-output-from-g53 rather than deleted.
defects.notes:
Not cleanup: a dirty tree makes closure.pin_target refuse, so a bench run can block the closure-target freeze, and a stray directory at the repo root is easily swept into a commit by `git add -A`.
OPEN, not closed: the exact call path is NOT reproducible without a paid real session — the fake-client path (`--tu-kiem`) was tried and does not reproduce it, so the trigger lies in real agent behaviour inside a session. Claiming a fix I cannot verify would be worse than leaving this open.
What did ship is the deterministic part: `ro_ri_ngoai_workspace` snapshots the framework root before a run and names anything the run left behind, turning a silent leak into a loud one at the point it happens, with red-first tests and a negative control for a directory that already existed. P2 and non-blocking: it changes no gate verdict and loses no evidence.
2026-09-15, Column-2 containment verified: the boundary check ran after every one of the 12 tasks in both arms (snapshot taken before the run so a pre-existing directory is not blamed on it) and never fired. After 72 attempts and 5.5 session-hours the framework repository is clean — `git status --porcelain` empty, HEAD unchanged, no `_bmad-output` at the root. One out-of-workspace write was ATTEMPTED and blocked: the guard's single `write-scope` block in the cohort names `aisef/phases/implement.py`, i.e. a session tried to write into the real repository and was stopped. So containment held under the heaviest run this project has done. Root cause still not reproduced and still P2/POST_CLOSE: reproducing it needs a paid session, and the owner's standing instruction is not to spend model calls solely to reproduce a P2. Worth noting for whoever picks it up: `bat_buoc_ranh_gioi` watches only `_bmad-output` at the root, so a write into `aisef/` would not be caught by it — in the AISEF arm the guard caught it, in the bare arm nothing would.

defects.title: verification applicability cannot be derived, so a blanket waiver is the only exit
defects.evidence: marks-cli pre-deploy left sit, api-contract, uat, perf, migration unconfigured with no way to say they do not apply, so release_ready required a 5-kind verify.waived. The framework's only applicability rule was Kind.needs_ui, covering 2 of 12 kinds.
defects.notes:
P1 because the only available exit degraded assurance: a blanket waiver cannot distinguish 'does not apply' from 'forgot to configure', which is the signal the gate exists to keep.
Fixed from structured, already-approved sources — each story's verification_contract, and covers against the PRD's requirement ids — never from requirements prose, since prose sniffing is defect 163. A kind no story declares on a plan covering every requirement is NOT_APPLICABLE with evidence; if any requirement is uncovered the answer is UNRESOLVED and blocks, which is the safety net for 'perf declared N/A merely because nobody configured a threshold'.
EXTENDED 2026-09-14 after the owner's adversarial audit, which was right: the first rule let a plan's omission prove the omission unnecessary — circular, and silent. Four negative controls were red: a PRD stating 'p95 latency under 200 ms' still made perf NOT_APPLICABLE; an openapi.yaml still made api-contract NOT_APPLICABLE; a migrations/ directory still made migration NOT_APPLICABLE; screens in design artefacts still made accessibility NOT_APPLICABLE.
Fixed with an explicit authority order: requirement / architecture / project capability outranks configured command, which outranks an approved story verification_contract, which outranks project-shape inference. A higher authority that demands a kind returns APPLICABLE and the kind then blocks as unconfigured until someone decides — never NOT_APPLICABLE.
Capability evidence is file presence first (openapi/proto/graphql, migrations//*.sql/prisma, Dockerfile, docker-compose) and requirement wording second. The wording patterns are deliberately liberal because the error direction is asymmetric: a wrong demand costs a human decision, a wrong dismissal loses a required property silently. That is the opposite of defect 163, where a loose match wrongly imposed browser checks.
mutation is separated as policy-optional: no AISEF policy requires it, so NOT_APPLICABLE is honest, but the recorded reason is 'no AISEF policy requires mutation' rather than 'no story asked for it'.
Re-derived on marks-cli: the demand scan finds nothing for sit, api-contract, uat, perf, migration, e2e, accessibility or mutation, and finds `Dockerfile` for image-scan — which is therefore APPLICABLE and actually runs, passing with zero findings.

defects.title: a verification tool must join the product's dependency tree to run
defects.evidence: Every kind ran in image_for(project), one image for all. Installing @stryker-mutator/core into marks-cli to run mutation pulled qs and typed-rest-client transitively and raised npm audit from 0 to 2 moderate advisories; reverted. Separately, image-scan was reported as blocked because trivy was not installed in the project image.
defects.notes:
P1: it forces a real choice between running a quality check and keeping the product's security posture, and the posture is what the product exists to demonstrate.
Fixed with `verify.tool_images` (kind=image) plus SandboxSpec.entrypoint, so each kind may run in its own pinned, disposable tool image while the product keeps zero runtime dependencies. The image's entrypoint is cleared because a verify command is a full command line — aquasec/trivy has ENTRYPOINT ['trivy'], which would otherwise run `trivy trivy fs`.
Proven end to end: marks-cli image-scan now runs `trivy fs --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --scanners vuln,secret` in aquasec/trivy:0.58.1 under the sandbox's own hardening (--cap-drop=ALL, --user 1000:1000, read-only workspace) and passes with zero findings. The network trivy uses to fetch its vulnerability database is not network granted to the application under verification.

defects.title: whole-plan acceptance scope cannot be declared, only implied
defects.evidence: marks-cli: 7/7 stories done, pre-deploy PASS, yet G4.6 read FAILED — 'report declares no acceptance scope (--epic)'. probe_pre_deploy requires rep['scope']['epic'] and pre_deploy left scope None whenever --epic was absent.
defects.notes: None meant both 'the entire plan' and 'nothing declared'. The only way past the gate was --epic on one epic of four, which would have the signer accept a quarter of what they are actually accepting and contradicts G4.3's 'every planned story reached done'. The strongest scope must be statable, not merely implied. Fixed by declaring {'epic': 'all', 'stories': [every story], 'outside': []} when no epic is given; --epic keeps its narrowing meaning, asserted by a negative control.

defects.title: a relative AISEF_BENCH_DIR makes an entire benchmark cohort unrunnable, and the failures look like results
defects.evidence: Column-2 launch 2026-09-14: 72/72 attempts FAIL, 0 turns, 0 USD, every row carrying 'Failed to change directory to .bench-c2/'; no model call occurred. KEEP_DIR used the env value verbatim (relative) while the default ROOT/'.bench' is absolute. The failing command is the pre-registered one, verbatim, from BENCH-PREREGISTRATION-C2.md section 5.
defects.notes:
P1 rather than P2 because the failure is silent in the worst way: the 72 rows are written to results.jsonl with outcome FAIL, so the cohort reads as 'AISEF 0/36, bare 0/36' — an infrastructure failure indistinguishable from a measured negative result. A reader reconstructing the experiment later would have drawn a conclusion from nothing.
Fixed by anchoring a relative value to ROOT, not Path.cwd(): a cohort belongs to the repository, not to wherever the operator happened to stand. Absolute values and the default are unchanged, each with a negative control.
The 72 rows are preserved under closure-evidence/c2-aborted-defect-170/ as evidence of the defect and removed from the cohort, because mixing them into results.jsonl would corrupt the real experiment. This is not rerunning a benchmark to improve its result: nothing ran and nothing was measured.
G5.3 unaffected: the qualification uses THU_MUC = ROOT/'.aisef-qual', hardcoded absolute and independent of AISEF_BENCH_DIR.

defects.title: bench session metrics merge cohorts, so a cut-session rate can belong to another experiment
defects.evidence: `_analyze._DUONG_DAN_PHIEN` matched `.bench*/run/<cond>/<task>/a<n>` but discarded the directory, so sessions from `.bench` (C-1), `.bench-c1b` and `.bench-c2` collapsed into one key space. Measured on C-2: 90 keys for a 72-attempt cohort, 18 belonging to no C-2 attempt, 198 sessions and 35 cut. Scoped per directory the truth is `.bench-c2` 72 sessions / 0 cut, `.bench` 95, `.bench-c1b` 36 — every cut session belonged to the two older cohorts. false_pass=true: the contaminated figures were published in docs/BENCH-REPORT-C2.md as 21%/14% and used to assert that G5.3's qualification had failed to predict production. Both statements were wrong and are corrected in §5 of that report.
defects.notes:
A second fault surfaced with it: one attempt (opencode/bug-a2-state-1/a1) vanished from the table because the model printed the path line-wrapped as `open-code`, `([\w-]+)` swallowed it, and the two-trees ambiguity rule dropped the session. Valid conditions now come from directories that exist on disk rather than from strings the model emitted. After both fixes C-2 reconciles exactly: 72 attempts, 72 sessions, 1:1, 0 unmapped, 0 missing.
false_pass=false deliberately, and the distinction matters: this was a false result of a CLOSURE PROBE / a bench metric, not of a gate CHECK_KIND. G2.4a's field is defined against CHECK_KIND, so recording it as a false PASS there would name a check that does not exist. The harm was real and is recorded in `evidence`; what it was not is a verification kind reporting green on red.

defects.title: a frozen early-stop rule was enforced only by the operator remembering it
defects.evidence: The frozen pre-registration says: two opening tasks at 6/6 across both arms means the model is at the dataset ceiling — stop, report, do not burn seven more hours. On C-2 `bug-a2-sec-4` and `bug-a2-sec-3` were both 6/6; the condition fired after task two and ten more tasks ran. The orchestrator held every Result needed to evaluate the rule, so this is an orchestration defect, not an operator slip.
defects.notes: Fixed by making the rule data (`tests/bench/stop_rule.json`, carrying its source and the source's digest) evaluated after each task by `_runner.kiem_dung_som`, with the decision written to `stop-decision.json`. Continuing past a fired rule now requires `--ignore-stop-rule` and is recorded with `honoured=false` and the post-stop label. Completed data is never discarded. Red-first: with the check disabled 3 of the 5 regressions fail. C-2 is NOT re-run — its result stands, layered into a confirmatory result and post-stop exploratory data.

defects.title: the retired-claim audit matched substrings, so it both missed and invented violations
defects.evidence: False negative: the matcher knew `±0.08` and not `±0,08`, so the same retired band restated with a decimal comma passed. False positive: docs/BENCH-REPORT-C2.md explains why `±0.08` was withdrawn and the probe read the explanation as the claim. Same shape as AD-22's grep failing on `"http://"` inside URL validation — a substring cannot tell asserting from mentioning.
defects.notes:
Replaced by declared status: a `claim_registry` in the criteria file lists retired claims with every surface form, and prose fences a non-assertion with `<!-- claim:WITHDRAWAL_EXPLANATION -->`. Anything outside a region, inside a CURRENT_ASSERTION region, or inside an unterminated region is an assertion. The audit surface also grew from 4 to 8 to include the BENCH-* reports the contract always said it covered.
false_pass=false deliberately, and the distinction matters: this was a false result of a CLOSURE PROBE / a bench metric, not of a gate CHECK_KIND. G2.4a's field is defined against CHECK_KIND, so recording it as a false PASS there would name a check that does not exist. The harm was real and is recorded in `evidence`; what it was not is a verification kind reporting green on red.

defects.title: CI checks out shallow, so tests that rebuild a historical commit error instead of running
defects.introduced: with the G5.3 qualification pipeline tests (5388ffb), after v1.6.0
defects.evidence: v1.7.0 release run 34908370558 failed: 4 errors, all `subprocess.CalledProcessError: ['git','archive','--format=tar', 'db0081275046d687e136bc2540cae78a156e7dd1'] exit 128`. That SHA is bug-a2-multi-2's `task.base` -- a commit in this repository's own history that `R.materialize` rebuilds on purpose. No workflow declared `fetch-depth`, so actions/checkout@v4 cloned at depth 1 and the commit was absent. The same suite at the same commit is green locally (3056/0) because the full history is present. CI ran 3072 tests, errors=4.
defects.notes:
Scope: PRODUCT RUNTIME WAS NOT BROKEN. The wheel built, twine passed, and `aisef --version` reported 1.7.0 from the target's own wheel. What was broken is the release CI environment, and the release gate did its job -- `publish` was skipped and no invalid package reached PyPI, which still served 1.6.0.
Why it surfaced only at v1.7.0: TestDuongOngTuyenCap arrived after v1.6.0 and remote master was 56 commits behind local, so the tag push was those tests' first CI exposure. v1.6.0's release run was green.
Fixed in the environment, not the test (owner ruling: option A): `fetch-depth: 0` on the checkout of every job that runs `unittest discover` -- tests.yml::unit and release.yml::build. No skip was added and no materialization coverage was weakened. Two static regressions in tests/test_meta.py, red-first verified: one asserts any job running the whole suite declares full-history checkout (anchored on the COMMAND, so a new job is caught too), the other resolves the task's base commit with `git cat-file` so a truncated history fails loudly rather than silently.
v1.7.0 is preserved as historical evidence: the remote tag stays on 966add6b484b4b7444c6913b2d45466e2f61137a, never moved or recreated, and the corrected candidate ships as 1.7.1. Failure artefacts kept at closure-evidence/v1.7.0-release-failure.log and v1.7.0-release-attempt.json, not rewritten.

defects.title: two POSIX assumptions in test helpers made 16 Windows tests fail once CI could reach them
defects.introduced: with the closure gate (575bb02) and the G5.3 pipeline (5388ffb), both after the old remote master
defects.evidence:
CI run 34913237817, job `unit (windows-latest, 3.11)`: Ran 3074 tests, failures=10 errors=6, while all four ubuntu jobs, lint and wheel were green. Two root causes and nothing else.
(A) 13 failures in test_closure.py TestApproval/TestCli/TestPin, all reading `contract is stale`. The Repo helper pinned sha256 over CONTRACT with `\n` but wrote the file with `write_text(..., encoding='utf-8')`, whose default newline translation emits `\r\n` on Windows -- so the digest of the bytes on disk could never match the pin.
(B) 3 failures in tests/bench (selfcheck + TestDuongOngTuyenCap) with `FileNotFoundError: calls.jsonl`. The fake `opencode` is a Python script written with a shebang and chmod 0o755; Windows does not honour shebangs, so the adapter could not launch it, no session wrote its log, and every attempt read as `hạ tầng` (infra).
defects.notes:
Neither is a product defect -- both are test-harness portability bugs -- and neither had ever run on Windows CI: both files arrived after the old remote master (9a91f9c), which sat 56 commits behind. The previous Windows run failed on exactly one unrelated test (test_memory.test_concurrent_writers), which passes now.
Fixed, not skipped. (A) `Repo.write` uses `newline=''` so the platform cannot rewrite the bytes a digest is taken over. (B) one helper `_selfcheck.viet_client_gia()` now materialises the fake client for all three call sites, and on Windows writes `opencode.py` plus a one-line `opencode.bat` launching the running interpreter -- same script, same stream, only the way the OS starts it differs. The three sites had duplicated the write-and-chmod, which is why one platform bug could appear three times.
Found only because D-019's `fetch-depth: 0` let the suite reach these tests at all.

defects.title: a pin key and a reported path carry the platform's separator, so the same file has two identities
defects.evidence: CI run 34915208534, Windows job: two failures, both the same shape. `pin()` recorded `{'docs\\\\BENCH-PREREGISTRATION-C2.md': ...}` because it built the key with `str(path.relative_to(root))`, and the CLI printed `docs\\\\CLOSURE-REPORT.md` where `closure.REPORT_MD` is the documented `docs/CLOSURE-REPORT.md`.
defects.notes:
The pin half is the serious one and it is a PRODUCT defect, not a test defect: the key goes into `docs/closure-gate.json`, which is committed and shared. A pin written on Windows would not be found by a probe reading it on Linux -- one file, two identities, and the mismatch is silent. The printed path is cosmetic but was inconsistent with the constant it is supposed to echo.
Both fixed with `as_posix()` rather than `str()`. Regression `test_pinned_keys_are_posix_on_every_platform` asserts no key carries a backslash and each equals its own as_posix form. Stated plainly in its docstring: on POSIX the assertion is nearly tautological because as_posix() and str() coincide, so its proving power lives in the Windows CI job -- which is real and runs, so this is a genuine check rather than a decorative one.
Third defect in the chain that only became visible once D-019 let the suite run: 16 Windows failures became 2, and those 2 were a real cross-platform product bug underneath.

defects.title: release identity conflated with repository HEAD: recording post-release evidence invalidated the release
defects.evidence: Measured on this repository 2026-09-15: v1.7.1 published at 5c5ba52, G1 PASSED (64deed9); commit 8b3eada synced public docs (docs/*.md, landingpage/, SALEKIT.html) and touched nothing that ships; G1.0 read FAILED 'HEAD is 0e68b96, closure targets 5c5ba52'. Red-first regression tests/test_release_identity.py::TestV1AFixedPoint: 2 of 5 red against the old probe (an external-validation report commit and a documentation-sync commit both invalidated the release), the negative control (a runtime change still blocks) green.
defects.notes:
A closure ARCHITECTURE defect, not a probe bug: the exception `_only_bookkeeping_changed` was a filename allowlist (closure-evidence/ and the criteria file) standing in for a model of what the product is. Any evidence outside those two places -- an external-validation record, a handoff sheet, a doc sync -- moved HEAD and made G1 red, so release R needed release R+1 to be closable, whose evidence would need R+2. No fixed point.
Fixed by stating the model (`aisef/control/planes.py`, rules in docs/closure-gate.json#planes): a PRODUCT plane (runtime source, package data, build config) identified by a content digest over the tag's tree and by the PyPI artifact digests, and an ASSURANCE plane (tests, evidence, records) allowed to move after publication. G1.0 compares product identity between the release commit and HEAD; commit-bound evidence is stale only when a PRODUCT or ASSURANCE path changed; a path no rule classifies is UNRESOLVED and blocks. Release manifest per version records release_source_sha, product digests and the artifacts observed on PyPI with every member compared to the tag's blobs. Fixed-point invariant kept as a permanent test: release R -> validate R -> record -> close R converges without R+1 unless the product identity changes.
P1: it blocked closure outright and could only be escaped by a release that would re-create it. false_pass=false: it produced false FAILEDs, never a pass.

defects.title: G6.1 read the onboarding digest under a key its writer never wrote (latent false FAIL)
defects.introduced: 7a450ce (onboarding digest module) alongside the older probe
defects.evidence: closure-evidence/onboarding-digest.json is written by `aisef.control.onboarding` with the value under `digest` and no `version` field; `closure.probe_external_report` read `rec.get('sha256')` and `rec.get('version')` and recomputed the digest with a second implementation (`closure.onboarding_digest`, whitespace-normalised prose) that differs from the recorded one (commands + defaults only). With a record present the probe would have read version '' -> FAILED 'different MAJOR.MINOR', and with that fixed, '' != digest -> FAILED 'onboarding surface changed'. Latent only because no record existed yet (G6 UNRUNNABLE hid it).
defects.notes: Two implementations of one digest and two spellings of one key -- the class J shape ('two rules for one truth'). Fixed by deleting the probe's copy: G6.1 now reads the record and recomputes through `aisef.control.onboarding.compute_onboarding_digest`, the function that wrote it. The MAJOR.MINOR clause of ruling 4 is subsumed by G6.1's exact release binding (adjustment 8). false_pass=false: it would have blocked, not passed; P1 because closure could not have completed without an author fixing the gate.

defects.title: bench-qualification test helper: TemporaryDirectory cleanup races a writer inside a session's .git (twice: 3.13, 3.14)
defects.introduced: unknown -- first seen on CI run 34925033781, first attempt, ubuntu-latest/3.13
defects.evidence: tests/test_bench_qualification.py::TestDuongOngTuyenCap::test_moi_phien_co_cay_lam_viec_rieng: assertions passed, then `_tra_lai` -> TemporaryDirectory.cleanup() raised OSError [Errno 39] Directory not empty: .../q/run/opencode/bug-a2-multi-2/s2/.git (Python 3.13 _rmtree_safe_fd: an entry appeared between scandir and rmdir). Same commit (d092b25): 3.11, 3.12, 3.14 and Windows green; the 3.13 job re-run green; locally 0/30 failures on 3.12 and 3.14. The commit under test touched no bench code. Second occurrence 2026-09-15: CI run 34968979318 (push of cfee273, ubuntu-latest/3.14) — tests/test_bench_qualification.py::TestDuongOngTuyenCap::test_dung_som_khi_cap_khong_con_dat_duoc, OSError [Errno 39] Directory not empty: .../q/run/opencode/bug-a2-multi-2/s1/.git; the same commit had passed all seven jobs on the pull_request run 34966086751 minutes earlier; the failed job was re-run.
defects.notes:
A test-infrastructure race, not a product defect and not a gate defect: it fires after the test's assertions, in cleanup. The writer is not identified -- the fake opencode client and materialize() both finish synchronously, git gc --auto is far below its threshold on a ~600-object repo, and the CI log carries no background-git message -- so no fix is claimed. Recorded rather than papered over with ignore_cleanup_errors, which would hide the writer for good. Re-open as P2 if it recurs; then capture `ls -la .git` and `ps` at cleanup time in the helper.
2026-09-15 later, macOS 3.14, HEAD 7e34467: one full `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q` run ended `FAILED (failures=1, skipped=19)` — an assertion failure this time, not a cleanup error — with the test name lost to a `tail -3`; the immediate re-run of the same command passed 3122/OK, and the two modules changed since 1.7.2 pass alone. Two symptoms, one observation each, name unknown for the second: still P3, but the next full run must capture complete output so a name can be attached. Raised to P2 on the second occurrence, as this entry said it should be. Still a test-infrastructure race in the assurance plane (a different test of the same class, a different interpreter, the same directory shape); the writer is still unidentified. Next step remains the one written here: capture `ls -la .git` and `ps` at cleanup time in the helper.

defects.title: review execution failure scored as a review verdict: story re-enters the developer stage and dies by the no-op policy
defects.introduced: review_story_v2 'review could not run' finding (1.4.x) + no-op policy MAX_NOOP (1.6.x, lỗi 127); first observed on public 1.7.3
defects.evidence: closure-evidence/dogfood/ledgerlock-run2/F-A.json (LedgerLock Run #2, 2026-09-15, aisef 1.7.3 from PyPI, STORY-01-06 candidate eed6f87a); regression: tests/test_run2_review_recovery.py (red on 1.7.3, green on 1.7.4) — 6 tests + 2 subtests RED on master before the fix (retry on the same candidate; persistent failure ends REVIEW_UNRUNNABLE not as a developer no-op; candidate preserved and every review execution recorded; incomplete prior review not reused by verify-only, legacy and current shape; verify-only names REVIEW_UNRUNNABLE when cut again; resume at the review stage without a developer; resume with the budget spent ends REVIEW_UNRUNNABLE), 6 controls GREEN (genuine block, lint failure and test failure return to the developer; retries bounded; completed prior review reused).
defects.notes: Deterministic gates green, security clean, reviewer cut at max_turns with no verdict → 'review could not run' stored as a blocking review finding → gate FAILED review → the loop's only recovery is a new developer attempt → the developer correctly writes nothing → the tree already carries a gate:verdict → NO-OP → after two, terminal. A forced resume repeats it. Two rules for one truth: 'the reviewer said no' and 'the reviewer did not run' share one slot. Required semantics (owner, 2026-09-15): retain the candidate, bounded REVIEW retry, end in PASS / structured BLOCK / explicit REVIEW_UNRUNNABLE. Fixed in 1.7.4 (narrow patch, D-032 only): aisef/phases/implement.py — review outcomes REVIEW_PASS/REVIEW_BLOCK/REVIEW_UNRUNNABLE, review_story_v2 returns the execution failure separately from findings, verify_candidate records outcome/unrunnable/review_attempt per execution against the candidate SHA and reuses prior review evidence only when it holds a completed verdict (the 1.7.3 shape `review could not run:` counts as incomplete), _review_stage re-runs only the review on the same candidate up to MAX_REVIEW_RETRIES=2 more times and ends the story REVIEW_UNRUNNABLE, _pending_review resumes at the review stage without a developer, verify_only names REVIEW_UNRUNNABLE, a reviewer commit (candidate moved) is an execution failure and the worktree is reset to the frozen candidate before the retry (tests/test_candidate.py and tests/test_implement.py reviewer-integrity expectations adapted); aisef/control/gate.py — review_unrunnable scores `review` UNRUNNABLE, never FAILED, and judge_only excludes it; aisef/phases/run.py — journal review.completed records outcome, review_executions, developer_attempts.

defects.title: a resumed story re-baselined at its own candidate: renaming its own tests was scored as a baseline regression
defects.introduced: run_baseline once per implement_story invocation at the worktree HEAD (ADR-004 R9, 1.4.x) + _baseline_check reading the newest test:baseline record; first observed on the clean OpenCode replay of LedgerLock Run #2 on public 1.7.4
defects.evidence: closure-evidence/dogfood/ledgerlock-run2/replay-1.7.4-opencode/REPLAY-OPENCODE.json (OBS-OC-1, owner diagnostic 2026-09-16: STORY-03-01 baseline seq 393 parent ca37cc44 vs story-entry seq 2 parent 9cf22f5c; verify-only verdict evidence [393, 1694]; the two 'lost' tests did not exist at 9cf22f5 and were written by the story in bdc21244); regression: tests/test_baseline_provenance.py (red on 1.7.4, green on 1.7.5) — 10 red on master before the fix (E, F, G2, H gate cases; A, B, C, G, H producer cases; I detection count), 4 controls green (entry baseline alone; no record at all stays NOT_APPLICABLE; verify-only records no baseline; G gate selection)
defects.notes: Owner invariant (2026-09-16): the authoritative baseline is captured from the integrated parent at story entry; retries, resumes and verify-only reuse that exact record; a candidate produced by the story never becomes its baseline; a new baseline only for a new story epoch, from the integrated parent; absent or provenance-invalid → fail closed. Fixed in 1.7.5 (narrow patch): aisef/control/acceptance.py contract_fingerprint (story epoch, shared with run.py's story:contract note); aisef/phases/implement.py run_baseline captures once per (story, epoch) at the integrated parent with root/epoch recorded, reuses on retry/resume ('baseline REUSED'), records BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE (unrunnable) instead of baselining a resumed story's own HEAD; the nop control's parent fallback uses the same selection; aisef/control/gate.py authoritative_baseline selects the story-entry record for the current epoch (records without epoch accepted only at the branch point and after the current contract note), _baseline_check fails closed (UNRUNNABLE BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE) when records exist but none is authoritative, _nop_check uses the same selection. A correct candidate could not complete the lifecycle without operator intervention → P1 under the D-032 rule; fail-closed, no false pass. Secondary (backlog, not changed): _class_of rename heuristic does not recognise pytest node-id renames — no independent red against the correct baseline.
